idea.research_question: How can harmonized Sentinel-2 and Landsat time series combined with ASTER terrain variables distinguish mountain permafrost landscape units?
idea.hypothesis: Phenological spectral trajectories from Sentinel-2 and Landsat, when combined with terrain and elevation, provide sufficient information to separate tundra, forest and intrazonal valley landscape units.
idea.mechanism: Monthly optical composites yield NDVI, GNDVI and NDMI phenology features; the Landsat series extends temporal context; ASTER GDEM-derived relief and landform variables encode the topographic organization of permafrost landscapes. A supervised classifier maps these joint ecological and geomorphological units.

key_variables.target: Mountain permafrost landscape class and landscape-structure statistics
predictors: ASTER GDEM elevation, relief and landform variables

idea.analytical_approach: Phenological compositing and feature engineering, multisensor harmonization, SVM or random-forest classification, followed by landscape-diversity and hypsometric-profile analysis.
idea.expected_contribution: A reproducible multisensor method for mapping and comparing the spatial organization of mountain permafrost landscapes.
idea.falsification_condition: Adding temporal optical features or terrain variables does not improve class separability over a single-date or single-sensor baseline, or predicted classes fail independent map/field comparison.
